security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences or expected IaC file generation examples. Confirmed risks include an unpinned remote Argo CD manifest, a hardcoded Flux installer URL, and a critical curl-to-bash pattern. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Remote Flux install script is piped into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-bash example with a package manager, signed release artifact, pinned version, and checksum verification.

remediation.issue: Deployment hooks execute through bash from application configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Remove shell=True for hooks. Use allowlisted commands with structured argument arrays and reject repository-controlled shell strings.

remediation.issue: The Argo CD install example applies a remote manifest from an unpinned URL.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the manifest to a specific release tag or digest and require review before applying it to a cluster.

remediation.issue: Generated IaC files overwrite fixed filenames in the selected working directory.
remediation.suggestion: Document that examples should run in an isolated workspace and should fail before overwriting existing files unless explicitly approved.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Deployment Hook Shell Execution
semantic_findings.description: The GitOps example reads deployment hooks from application configuration and executes each hook through bash. A copied implementation could run arbitrary shell commands from repository-controlled configuration.

content.value_statement: Cloud teams need repeatable patterns for infrastructure, deployment, and release safety. This skill provides practical IaC, GitOps, and progressive delivery guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Defines Terraform and Pulumi backend patterns for generated infrastructure files.
Shows multi-cloud deployment management with provider abstraction and failover concepts.
Describes Argo CD and Flux GitOps initialization, synchronization, and deployment flows.
Explains rolling, canary, and blue-green delivery strategies for Kubernetes applications.
Models canary analysis with metrics, thresholds, traffic steps, and rollback decisions.
limitations: It provides reference patterns, not a packaged deployment runtime.
Examples need review before use in production clusters or cloud accounts.
It does not include complete provider modules for every cloud service.
Some install examples must be replaced with pinned and verified alternatives.

use_cases.title: Plan a Platform Foundation
use_cases.description: Design shared IaC, GitOps, and release patterns before building an internal developer platform.

use_cases.title: Standardize Multi-Cloud Delivery
use_cases.description: Compare provider abstraction, failover, and deployment options across cloud environments.

use_cases.title: Review Progressive Release Safety
use_cases.description: Assess canary, blue-green, and rollback controls before changing production release workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Map an IaC Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new service environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cloud-native skill to outline an Infrastructure as Code baseline for a small Kubernetes service. Include provider choice, state management, validation, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a GitOps Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cloud-native skill to design a GitOps workflow for three environments. Compare Argo CD and Flux, and include synchronization, rollback, and access controls.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Release Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cloud-native skill to evaluate canary and blue-green deployment options for a high-traffic API. Include metrics, traffic steps, failure thresholds, and rollback triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Platform Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cloud-native skill to create a platform blueprint across IaC, GitOps, progressive delivery, policy checks, and observability. Call out operational risks and manual approval gates.

output_examples.input: Plan a GitOps workflow for staging and production.
output: A repository and environment layout for declarative application delivery.
A comparison of Argo CD and Flux responsibilities.
A rollout plan with sync checks, manual approvals, and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: Review a canary deployment plan for an API.
output: Recommended traffic increments and analysis windows.
Health and business metrics to watch during rollout.
Clear rollback conditions when error rate or latency exceeds limits.

output_examples.input: Create an IaC operating model for a platform team.
output: A division of responsibilities between platform and application teams.
State, secrets, validation, and change review requirements.
A rollout path from development environments to production accounts.

best_practices: Pin tool versions and validate manifests before applying them to a cluster.
Run generated IaC examples in isolated working directories and review plans before apply.
Replace free-form deployment hooks with allowlisted command templates.
anti_patterns: Do not copy remote install scripts that pipe directly into a shell.
Do not run Terraform or Pulumi apply steps without human review in production.
Do not mix production and test cluster credentials while testing examples.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Terraform, Pulumi, Argo CD, Flux, Kubernetes workflows, and general platform engineering patterns.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it deploy infrastructure automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and examples. Users must run and secure any generated implementation themselves.

faq.question: Is it tied to one cloud provider?
faq.answer: No. It is written as a framework-agnostic guide for multi-cloud and hybrid environments.

faq.question: What should I review before using examples?
faq.answer: Review remote install commands, shell hooks, auto-approve deployment flags, credentials, and cluster targets.

faq.question: Who is the primary audience?
faq.answer: It is most useful for platform engineers, DevOps architects, and site reliability engineers.
